_note: Errands. `giver` is who asks and `turn_in` is who takes it back — the two differ whenever somebody sends you to tell somebody else, which is the shape half the first map's errands have. `requires` names errands that must be done first, and a questline is that and nothing else. Every reward is a component that is on no shelf and drops from nothing: an errand you could have shopped your way past is a slow shop.

quests.name: THE EYES HAVE IT
quests.brief: A clerk in the pit's own office keeps the register of what lives here. Bengulon jungle toads are not on it, and are four streets in. Nine planes over is where they are from; somebody brought forty and did not stay. She will not write down a thing she has not been handed, and what she will accept is eyes. Five toads. Ten eyes, which she is counting as five.
quests.thanks: She writes for a while. Then she gives you a ledger with a spine like a brick and a page of counting-out that she says works, and has not said on what. The register now runs to a hundred and nine species and one line that says PENDING.

quests.name: THE ONES STILL DOWN THERE
quests.brief: Four hundred Sprocketmen are still in the workings and the office is not permitted to send anything down that could be called a wage. Tins are not a wage. The clerk would like four Long Shift Tins, bought with your own Fnorp, handed to her across the counter, and entered in the register as a donation of nothing.
quests.thanks: She writes DONATION: NIL, four times, and stacks the tins behind the counter where the register cannot see them. Then she gives you a frame with somebody's counting scratched into the inside of it — four numbers, each smaller than the last.

quests.name: SOMEBODY SHOULD TELL HIM
quests.brief: The register has a line for the cork fence and the line says GOING WEST, A HAND A YEAR. The clerk would like somebody to walk out to the man cutting through it and tell him that the office is aware, that the office has been aware since the fourth doorway, and that being aware is the whole of what the office intends to do.
quests.thanks: He takes it well. He says he had assumed as much and has been cutting on that assumption for nine doorways. Then he gives you the knife, which is not a gift so much as a handover, and starts on the tenth with a piece of the fence.

quests.name: THE COUNT IS WRONG
quests.brief: The board by the heap has been corrected four times and each correction is smaller. Somebody is counting a pile that is going down and writing the number as though the pile is the thing that changed. The office keeps a register. The office should be told there is a heap on the slag that is eleven thousand teeth and falling, and that nobody is standing near it.
quests.thanks: The clerk writes it into the register under a heading she has to invent, reads it back twice, and gets quieter. Then she gives you a strip of the fence out of a drawer, which she says grows back, and which she says the office is aware of.

quests.name: THE FIRST THING SHE WANTS
quests.brief: "Whisperlings," says Marbulon. "Three. Not because I want anything off them — I want to know whether there are three left, and the only way to know that is somebody comes back and says there are not." She does not say what she will do with the answer. She has the key in her apron and she takes it out while she is talking and puts it back.
quests.thanks: "Three," she says. "So there were three." She writes nothing down. Then she gives you a thimble that has been mended twice, and says the first thing is done and the second thing is worse.

quests.name: THE SECOND THING SHE WANTS
quests.brief: "Now go and look at the gate," she says. "Not through it. At it. Henpeck's people put cork over sneel over your own people's bracket work, and the bracket work is still holding the hinges, and I want somebody who has stood in front of that to be the one carrying my key." She is facing the door again. "Come back and tell me it is still standing."
quests.thanks: "Still standing," she repeats, and does not sound surprised. She gives you the key off her apron, and a piece of glass she says is ground for nine planes over and works best on this one. Then she turns the chair to face the door and does not turn it back.

quests.name: A QUIVER OF NOCKS
quests.brief: The fletcher at Kettleworks has been buying arrows back off the wallspider swarms for six years and has never once got a nock returned with them. He has a drawer of eight hundred shafts and nothing to put on the end of any of them. Four nocks. He is not asking where they come from and neither should you.
quests.thanks: He fits one, looks down the shaft, and puts it in the drawer with the other eight hundred. Then he gives you a frame and a visor off the shelf behind him, which was not on the shelf in front of him, and does not explain the difference.

quests.name: THE LONG MIRROR INVENTORY
quests.brief: High Wick keeps an inventory of everything the Yodregar Archive has reflected, on the grounds that a thing seen twice has been in the world twice. The inventory is nine volumes and none of them agree. Three shards, and the clerk will start volume ten, which she says will be the last one, as she has said of the previous four.
quests.thanks: She holds a shard up, looks at what is behind her in it, and writes for eleven minutes. Volume ten is open. Then she hands you an ink and a word she says goes with it, and adds that neither is in the inventory and she would rather they stayed out of it.

quests.name: THE FRAME THAT STANDS
quests.brief: The register has a Sprocketman frame standing in the Burnwarp with nothing in it, and has had for thirty years. The clerk wants somebody to go and look at it, because the entry says EMPTY and an entry that has said the same thing for thirty years is an entry nobody has checked. She would like it checked.
quests.thanks: She writes STILL EMPTY, and the date, and looks at it for a while. Then she goes into the back and comes out with a card in a sleeve. It is nine lines of somebody working out what a thing they were holding was for, and it was not filed under gear, and she says the office has no heading it goes under either.

quests.name: A DOOR WHERE THERE WAS NOT ONE
quests.brief: The register has a line for the western wall and the line has said ROCK, NINE MILES, NO OPENINGS for a hundred and four years. Somebody came in this morning and said there is a door in it. The clerk would like that either confirmed or taken back, and she would like it confirmed by whoever is carrying the Cave's key, because she has worked out which of those two facts came first.
quests.thanks: She writes ONE OPENING, and the date, and under it the words AS OF TODAY, which she says is the only honest way to file a thing that was not there yesterday. Then she pays you out of a drawer she has to unlock, and says the office has no procedure for what is on the other side and will be inventing one.

quests.name: WHAT THE DOOR SMELLS OF
quests.brief: The works keeps a book on the Drambus Stack and the book has one gap in it, which is that nobody has written down what the door smells of. Four people have been sent and all four have come back and said it smells of cheese, and the clerk has refused all four on the grounds that the whole field smells of cheese. Go and stand at the door and come back with a better sentence.
quests.thanks: She writes what you said down without changing a word of it, reads it back, and says it is the fifth answer and the first one that is about the door. Then she gives you a layer off the shelf and says the works has nine of them and no shelf to put them on.

quests.name: WHAT COMES OFF IT
quests.brief: Things live in the Stack's shadow that do not live anywhere else in the field, and the works would like four of them counted properly rather than described. The clerk is specific: four of the ones that stand about in the crumb field with their hands together. Bring the count back and she will start the sixth book.
quests.thanks: Four counted, in a book that has been open at page one for two years. She writes the four in, rules the page off, and gives you a hall out of a crate that has KETTLEWORKS stencilled on it and a shipping label to somewhere else.

quests.name: THE FRAME IN THE SHALLOWS
quests.brief: There is a standing frame at the edge of this field and the works has been told there is a standing frame in the Bambulon shallows, and the works does not believe it. Eleven days each way. Go and stand at the one in the shallows and come back and say whether it is the same frame, and the clerk will accept either answer as long as you have been.
quests.thanks: "Two," she says, and writes it, and looks at it for a while. "Two is worse." Then she goes into the back and comes out with a head-measure in a sleeve, which she says came with the second book and has never fitted anybody at the works.

quests.name: THE COUNT AT THE POND
quests.brief: The man at the quench pond has 1,402 chalked on the rail and no idea what of. He has narrowed it to four possibilities and would like the fourth eliminated, which means four of the ones that come round the field counting things and writing none of it down. He will not tell you the other three possibilities. Take what you get to the clerk in town; he does not go in.
quests.thanks: The clerk reads the count, says the pond man has been at this for six years, and writes it in the book anyway. Then she gives you a wire off a reel that says MULTICITY on the flange and has nine feet left on it.

quests.name: THE DRAWER OF EIGHT HUNDRED
quests.brief: The fletcher counted eight hundred and one shafts on Tuesday and eight hundred and four today and has stopped having a theory. The clerk would like somebody who is not the fletcher to stand at the drawer and look at it. That is the whole errand. She is aware of how it sounds.
quests.thanks: "And?" she says, and then, before you answer, "No, do not. He will ask and I would rather not be able to tell him." She writes NOT KNOWN in the book, which is the first time that has been written in it, and gives you a length of rodding off the wall.

quests.name: THE NINE AND THE ELEVEN
quests.brief: The milestone at the field gate says Kettleworks eleven and the milestone on the Treyway says nine, and the woman who sits against the second one says the nine is a lie people tell about the marsh. The clerk wants it settled by somebody who has stood at the far end. Walk the road, find the post at the edge of the reach, and come back.
quests.thanks: She hears it out, crosses out neither number, and cuts a third line under both of them in the book. Then she gives you a ledger that is not the works' ledger and says it came off a cart nine years ago and has been waiting for somebody who walks.
